title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow?

items.stem: Which statement correctly separates a workflow from an agent?

options.text: A workflow calls tools, while an agent only writes text and calls no tools
A workflow makes one model call, while an agent makes several model calls
In a workflow, code fixes the steps; in an agent, the model picks the steps
A workflow runs on a smaller model, while an agent needs a stronger model

items.stem: Your booking feature always runs the same three steps in this order. Step 1: the model reads the student's message and extracts the machine, date and time. Step 2: your Python code calls the booking system. Step 3: the model writes a confirmation message. Which description fits this feature?

options.text: A workflow, because your code decides the order of the steps every time
An agent, because the model is called more than once for one request
An agent, because the feature ends up using a tool to book the slot
Neither, because the model and the code share the control of the steps

items.stem: Which part of the makerspace assistant is the best candidate for a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Working out why a student's 3D print keeps warping, using several manuals
Booking a slot: check training, check the calendar, write the booking, confirm
Investigating a vague report that "the laser cutter is acting weird today"
Answering unusual questions that may need any of the twelve machine manuals

items.stem: Assume every model call costs $0.02. A fixed workflow always makes 2 model calls per request. An agent doing the same job averages 6 model calls per request. Over 500 requests, how much more does the agent cost than the workflow, in dollars?

Your sponsor wants a guaranteed upper limit on the number of model calls per request, from the design alone and with no extra safeguard added. Which design can promise that: a workflow or an agent? Answer with one word.
Your team builds an agent and adds a limit of 8 steps per request, so the loop always ends. A teammate says this has turned it into a workflow. Is the teammate right?

options.text: Yes, because code now controls when the loop ends, so code owns the flow
Yes, because any system with a fixed upper bound on its steps is a workflow
No, because a workflow can only be built with a single model call per request
No, because the model still picks which action comes next within that limit
